recipes.name: Coq au Vin
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, winey and savoury, with chicken that falls from the bone into a glossy dark sauce studded with smoky lardons, mushrooms and small sweet onions.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken legs braised slowly give plenty of protein, and the mushrooms, onions and carrots add fibre and potassium to a rich dish best kept for a slow weekend meal.

ingredients.prepNote: a mature cockerel is the old way; legs are the usual choice now
a full bottle of red Burgundy

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Put the chicken in a bowl with the carrot, onion, garlic, thyme and bay leaves, pour the wine over and marinate in the fridge for 12 to 24 hours.
Lift out the chicken and pat it dry. Strain the marinade, keeping the wine and the vegetables separately.
In a heavy casserole, fry the lardons in a little oil until golden, 5 to 7 minutes, then lift them out. Brown the chicken in the fat in batches, 8 to 10 minutes a batch, and set aside.
Soften the marinade vegetables in the casserole for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 2 minutes. Return the chicken, warm the cognac, pour it over and flame it.
Pour in the wine and the warm stock, add the lardons back, bring to a simmer, cover and braise in the oven at 325 to 350°F (160 to 175°C) for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the meat is very tender.
Meanwhile brown the mushrooms in half the butter, 6 to 8 minutes, and glaze the pearl onions in the rest with a splash of water until tender, 10 to 15 minutes.

Lift out the chicken, boil the sauce until it coats a spoon, 5 to 10 minutes, and season it with the salt and pepper. Return the chicken with the mushrooms and onions, scatter with parsley and serve with boiled potatoes or bread.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carrots braised in the sauce.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Coq au vin

recipes.name: Poulet Basquaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright and gently warm, with tender chicken in a soft stew of sweet peppers, tomatoes and onion, salty ham and the mild heat of piment d'Espelette.
recipes.healthBenefit: The peppers and tomatoes bring a good amount of vitamin C and carotenoids beside the protein from the chicken, cooked in olive oil.

ingredients.prepNote: a green Basque pepper where you can find it
ground dried Espelette pepper, mild; 1.5 tsp at 2 g per tsp

instructions: Heat half the olive oil in a wide casserole and soften the onions and garlic over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Add the peppers and cook 10 minutes more, stirring now and then.
Add the ham, tomatoes, tomato paste, bay, thyme and the piment d'Espelette, and simmer this piperade uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile season the chicken with salt and brown it in the rest of the oil in a frying pan, 8 to 10 minutes, until golden on all sides.
Pour off the fat, deglaze the pan with the white wine and tip it all into the piperade. Nestle in the chicken, season with pepper, cover and simmer gently for 30 to 35 minutes.
Uncover and let the sauce reduce for 10 minutes. Taste for salt and Espelette, and serve with white rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the red and green peppers and the tomatoes.
From the chicken and the ham.
Tomatoes cooked down in olive oil.

recipes.curationNote: Mimi Thorisson, Basque chicken for every amount and step; serves 4 to 6: 1 chicken, 2 red and 1 green pepper, 2 onions, 4 garlic cloves, 230 g Bayonne ham, 6 tomatoes, 120 ml white wine, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 1 to 2 tsp Espelette, 2 bay leaves, a few sprigs of fresh thyme, olive oil, salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Poulet Rôti
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, salty, buttery skin over juicy meat, with a simple pan jus made from the drippings and a little water.
recipes.healthBenefit: A roast chicken is an everyday source of protein, B vitamins and selenium; the skin and butter make it richer, so the breast is the leaner part.

ingredients.prepNote: a poulet fermier if you can
a little in the dish, more for the jus
the source says to salt lightly, twice

instructions: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead and heat the oven to 410°F (210°C).
Set the bird in a roasting dish, rub it all over with butter, tuck small pieces under the wings and between the legs and breast, and drizzle with the oil.
Pour a thin layer of water into the dish, season the bird with pepper and lightly with salt, and roast for 45 minutes.
Baste generously with the juices, salt again, lower the oven to 350°F (180°C) and roast 30 to 45 minutes more, until the skin is golden and the juice from the thigh runs clear.
Rest the chicken on a board for 10 minutes. Stir a little hot water into the dish, scraping up the browned bits, and pour this jus into a jug.
Carve and serve with the jus, with frites, a green salad or potatoes roasted in the dish.

nutritionHighlights.note: Chicken meat, the breast especially, is rich in it.
Chicken is a steady everyday source.

recipes.curationNote: 750g, Poulet rôti au beurre for every amount and step; serves 4: a free-range chicken, butter, oil, water, salt lightly and pepper with no amounts; 45 minutes at 210°C then 30 to 45 at 180°C; no herbs.

recipes.name: Poulet Vallée d'Auge
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy and gently sweet with apple, cider and a breath of calvados, around tender chicken and smoky lardons.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives protein and the apples add a little fibre, while the butter and crème fraîche make this a rich dish.

ingredients.prepNote: crème fraîche d'Isigny if you can

instructions: Melt half the butter in a casserole and fry the lardons until golden, 5 minutes. Lift them out.
Season the chicken with the salt and pepper and brown it in the same fat, skin side down first, about 5 minutes. Add the onion, garlic and thyme and cook 10 minutes more, until soft and golden.
Pour in the calvados and let it bubble gently until the alcohol has cooked off.
Return the lardons, pour in the cider, bring to the boil, cover and simmer gently for 45 to 50 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Meanwhile fry the apple wedges in the remaining butter until golden and just soft, 8 to 10 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, stir the crème fraîche into the pan and heat through for about 5 minutes. Pour the sauce over the chicken, scatter with the parsley and serve with the apples.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the butter and crème fraîche.

recipes.curationNote: Complete France, Poulet Vallée d'Auge for every amount and step; 60 g butter, 125 g smoked lardons, 4 chicken legs, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp fresh thyme, 4 tbsp calvados, 500 ml dry cider, 100 g crème fraîche, 2 apples, 1 tbsp parsley, salt and pepper to taste; no mushrooms.

recipes.name: Confit de Canard
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, silky and deeply savoury, with meat that slides off the bone under skin crisped golden in the oven.
recipes.healthBenefit: Duck legs bring plenty of protein, iron and B vitamins; cooked and kept in fat, confit is rich and best eaten as a treat.

ingredients.prepNote: the legs cook covered in about 1 kg of duck fat, which is strained and kept; this is about what stays with the meat

instructions: Rub the duck legs well all over with the coarse salt, cover and refrigerate overnight, 12 to 24 hours.
Rinse the legs in cold water and pat them very dry.

Melt the duck fat in a heavy pot, add the legs with the garlic, thyme and bay, and cook very gently at 160 to 175°F (70 to 80°C), the fat barely trembling, for 2 to 3 hours, until the meat is tender to the bone.
Lift out the legs, strain the fat, then return the legs to a clean pot or jar and pour the fat over to cover them by about 1/2 inch (1.5 cm). Cool and keep refrigerated.
To serve, scrape off the fat and roast the legs skin side up at 400°F (200°C) for 25 to 30 minutes, or fry them skin side down until crisp and golden.
Serve with pommes sarladaises cooked in a spoonful of the fat, or with lentils and a green salad.

nutritionHighlights.note: Duck is a dark meat with more iron than chicken.
Duck fat is largely oleic acid, though it stays a rich fat.

citations.source: Mimi Thorisson, Confit de canard revisited

recipes.curationNote: Mimi Thorisson gives the overnight salt, 70 to 80°C cooking and the roasting finish; Wikipédia confirms cooking in its fat at 70 to 85°C for at least 2 hours and storing under fat. Only the fat that clings is counted, since the rest is strained and reused.

recipes.name: Magret de Canard
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, salty rendered fat over a rosy, tender breast that eats like a good steak.
recipes.healthBenefit: A duck breast is rich in protein, iron and B vitamins; much of the fat renders into the pan, though the skin still makes it a rich cut.

ingredients.cutPrep: one magret from a fattened duck, skin scored

ingredients.baseName: Fleur de sel, non iodée, non fluorée

instructions: Take the magret out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead. Score the skin in a crisscross with a sharp knife, cutting through the fat but not into the meat, and season both sides.
Lay it skin side down in a cold frying pan and turn the heat to medium, so the fat melts slowly.
Cook skin side down for 6 to 8 minutes, spooning off the fat as it gathers, until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Turn it and cook the flesh side for 2 to 4 minutes, to about 130 to 140°F (55 to 60°C) inside for pink.
Rest it for 5 minutes, then slice across into thick slices and serve with pommes sarladaises cooked in the rendered fat or a green salad.

nutritionHighlights.note: Duck breast is a red meat in all but name.
Duck meat is a good source.

citations.source: Croq'Kilos, La meilleure cuisson du magret de canard

recipes.curationNote: Croq'Kilos gives the cold pan start, 6 to 8 then 2 to 4 minutes, and the 55 to 60°C core; Wikipédia confirms the fat layer is kept and the meat served pink. Kept to salt and pepper as in Gascony.

recipes.name: Canard à l'Orange
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich roast duck under a glossy sauce that is bittersweet with caramel, orange and a touch of vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Duck brings protein and iron and the oranges a little vitamin C; with its skin and sauce this is a rich dish for an occasion.

ingredients.prepNote: zest of 2 oranges; bitter Seville oranges are the classic
juice of 2 oranges; from the 2 zested oranges

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Prick the duck skin all over, season inside and out with the salt and white pepper, rub with the butter and roast on a rack for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours, pouring off the fat every 20 minutes.
Blanch the julienned zest in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Melt the sugar in a small pan until it turns amber, 3 to 4 minutes. Take it off the heat and add the vinegar (stand back), then the shallot and the orange juice, and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the demi-glace and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the liqueur and the blanched zest.
Rest the duck 10 minutes, pour the fat from the roasting tin, deglaze it with a splash of the sauce and strain it back in. Warm the orange segments in the sauce.
Carve the duck and serve with the sauce spooned over and the segments around it.

nutritionHighlights.note: Duck is a dark, iron-rich meat.
From the orange juice and segments.

recipes.curationNote: The Reluctant Gourmet, Bigarade sauce for every amount and step; sauce: zest and juice of an orange, 1 tbsp shallot, 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 oz orange liqueur, ½ cup demi-glace, sugar only to correct bitterness, salt and white pepper to taste; Wikipédia gives the caramel, vinegar and orange gastrique.

recipes.name: Poulet Chasseur
recipes.flavorProfile: Savoury and herby, with browned chicken in a light tomato and white wine sauce full of mushrooms, shallots and tarragon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives protein and the mushrooms add B vitamins and selenium, in a sauce lighter than many French braises.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Season the chicken pieces with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide sauté pan and brown the chicken well on all sides, 10 to 12 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and shallots and let them colour with the chicken, 5 minutes.
Warm the cognac, pour it over and flame it, stirring until the flames die down.

Add the white wine and let it reduce by half, then the stock, tomato sauce and a bouquet garni of thyme, bay and parsley stalks. Cover and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Mash the butter and flour together. Lift out the chicken and the bouquet garni, whisk the butter paste into the sauce a little at a time and simmer 2 minutes until it thickens.
Pour the sauce over the chicken, scatter with tarragon, chervil and parsley and serve very hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: Chicken and mushrooms both bring it.

recipes.curationNote: iDealwine, Sauté de poulet chasseur for every amount and step; serves 4: 1.8 kg chicken, 250 g mushrooms, 3 shallots, bouquet garni, parsley, a little chervil and tarragon, 150 ml stock, 100 ml dry white wine, tomato, a small glass of cognac, a dessert spoon each of butter and flour, 4 tbsp oil, salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Bœuf Bourguignon
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, winey and deeply savoury, with beef soft enough to cut with a spoon in a glossy sauce of smoky lardons, mushrooms and shallots.
recipes.healthBenefit: Slow-braised chuck gives plenty of protein, iron and zinc, and the carrots and mushrooms add fibre and potassium to a rich dish meant for a long, slow meal.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: half to brown the beef, half for the garnish
1 small sprig, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Pat the beef dry. In a heavy casserole, fry the lardons until golden, 5 to 7 minutes, and lift them out.
Brown the beef in batches in the lardon fat with half the butter, 6 to 8 minutes a batch, and set aside.
Soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the casserole for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the beef and lardons, pour in the wine and the brown stock, tuck in the bouquet garni of thyme, bay and rosemary and bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in the oven at 325°F (160°C) for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the beef is very tender.

In the last 20 minutes, brown the mushrooms and shallots in the olive oil and the rest of the butter, 8 to 10 minutes, and stir them in. Remove the bouquet garni, season with the salt and pepper and serve with boiled potatoes or fresh pasta.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef chuck and lardons.
The beef carries most of it.
Slow-cooked beef is a good source.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Traditional beef bourguignon

recipes.name: Blanquette de Veau
recipes.flavorProfile: Gentle and creamy, with tender veal and mushrooms in a pale, silky sauce brightened with a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Poached veal gives lean protein and B vitamins, and the carrots and leeks cooked in the broth add vitamin A and fibre to a creamy dish best enjoyed in modest portions.

ingredients.cutPrep: tendron and shoulder, in 5 cm (2 in) pieces
2 tbsp for the mushrooms, 4 tbsp for the roux

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Put the veal in a large pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil and skim well for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots, onion, leek, garlic, bouquet garni and a little salt. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the veal is tender.
Meanwhile cook the mushrooms in 2 tbsp of the butter with a few drops of lemon until their liquid is gone, 6 to 8 minutes.

Lift out the veal and carrots and strain the broth. Melt the remaining butter, whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes without colouring, then whisk in 700 ml (about 3 cups) of the hot broth and simmer for 10 minutes.

Whisk the cream with the yolks and the rest of the lemon juice, stir in a ladle of the sauce, then pour it all back off the heat. Keep the sauce below about 150°F (65°C) from here so the yolks do not set.
Return the veal, carrots and mushrooms to the sauce, warm through gently and serve with white rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carrots poached with the meat.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Blanquette de veau

recipes.name: Pot-au-Feu
recipes.flavorProfile: Clean and comforting, with a clear beefy broth, meat that falls apart and soft winter vegetables eaten with coarse salt, mustard and cornichons.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef simmered for hours gives protein, iron and zinc, and the broth and plenty of root vegetables bring potassium and fibre in a dish that is gentle rather than rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: in one or two pieces, tied

ingredients.prepNote: added 10 minutes before serving; 1 each at 40 g per each; the marrow from one bone, about 40 g, is eaten

ingredients.cutPrep: coarse, plus more at the table

instructions: Rinse the beef, put it in a large pot with the cold water and bring slowly to a boil. Skim off the grey foam for about 10 minutes.
Add a handful of coarse salt and keep the pot at a bare simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots, turnips, leeks, celery, garlic, the onion with its cloves, the thyme and the parsley, and simmer for 2 hours more. Add the cabbage for the last 30 to 40 minutes.
Boil the potatoes separately in salted water until tender, 20 to 25 minutes, so they do not cloud the broth.
Slip in the marrow bone 10 minutes before serving.
Serve the strained broth first, then the sliced meat and vegetables with coarse salt, pepper, mustard and cornichons, and the marrow spread on toast.

nutritionHighlights.note: The potatoes, carrots and cabbage carry it.

recipes.curationNote: 750g, Pot au feu for every amount and step; serves 6: 800 g cheek or chuck, 700 g shin, 6 potatoes, 5 l water, 5 carrots, 1 marrow bone, 1 cabbage, 2 turnips, 1 onion, 2 leek whites, parsley, a sprig of thyme, 1 celery stalk, 2 garlic cloves, 2 cloves, a small handful of coarse salt, pepper; no bay leaf.

recipes.name: Daube Provençale
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep and fragrant, with beef braised for hours in red wine with orange peel, herbs and black olives into something dark and spoon-tender.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef cheek or chuck braised slowly gives protein, iron and zinc, and the olives and olive oil add mostly unsaturated fat to a rich, hearty stew.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: peel only, in 2 or 3 wide strips
sprigs, tied with the bay leaves and rosemary
sprigs, tied with the bay leaves and thyme

instructions: Put the beef in a bowl with the onions, carrots, celery, garlic, orange peel, cloves and a bouquet garni of the bay leaves, thyme and rosemary tied together, pour the wine over, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.
Lift out the beef and pat it dry; strain the marinade, keeping the wine and vegetables apart.
In a heavy casserole, brown the lardons in the olive oil, then the beef in batches, 6 to 8 minutes a batch.
Add the marinade vegetables and soften for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste and flour, then pour in the wine and the brown stock and bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in the oven at 250°F (120°C) for 4 to 5 hours, until the beef is very soft.
Stir in the olives for the last 15 minutes, lift out the bouquet garni, season with the salt and pepper and serve with fresh pasta, polenta or boiled potatoes.

nutritionHighlights.note: The beef carries most of it.
From the olives and olive oil.

recipes.name: Cassoulet
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, earthy and slow, with creamy white beans soaked in duck fat and pork juices under a crisp golden crust, studded with confit duck and sausage.
recipes.healthBenefit: White beans bring fibre, plant protein, folate and iron alongside the duck and pork, though with confit and sausage this is a heavy winter dish to share.

ingredients.prepNote: lingot beans if you can find them

instructions: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil for 5 minutes and drain again.
In a large casserole, warm the duck fat and brown the lardons and sausage pieces, 6 to 8 minutes. Lift them out.

Soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the fat for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then add the crushed tomatoes, white wine, beans, stock, the salt and pepper, and a bouquet garni of the rosemary, thyme and bay leaves.
Simmer gently for 1 hour, until the beans are just tender. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Layer the beans in a deep earthenware dish (a cassole) with the confit duck, lardons and sausage, finishing with beans, and add enough cooking liquid to come just to the top.
Bake uncovered for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, pushing the crust that forms back under a few times and adding liquid if it dries.
Scatter with the breadcrumbs and bake 30 minutes more, until deep golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: Beans, duck confit and pork together.
White beans are a good source.

recipes.name: Navarin d'Agneau
recipes.flavorProfile: Light and springlike, with tender lamb in a tomato-tinged sauce and sweet young turnips, carrots and peas.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lamb shoulder gives protein, zinc and vitamin B12, and the spring vegetables add vitamin A, vitamin C and fibre.

ingredients.cutPrep: bone in, in 5 cm (2 in) pieces

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: about 1 tbsp coarse salt, plus a little for the meat

instructions: Season the lamb with a little of the salt and the pepper and brown it in the oil in a heavy casserole, in batches, 6 to 8 minutes a batch. Pour off most of the fat.
Return the lamb with the onion, sprinkle with the flour and stir for 2 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and garlic.
Add water to just cover, the bay leaf and the rest of the salt and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook gently for 1 hour.
Add the turnips, carrots and potatoes and simmer 25 to 30 minutes more, until tender.
Add the peas for the last 5 to 8 minutes, skim off any fat, scatter with parsley and serve.

The potatoes and peas follow Wikipédia's description of the spring version.

recipes.name: Steak au Poivre
recipes.flavorProfile: Seared, peppery and luxurious, with a hot crushed-pepper crust and a creamy cognac pan sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef fillet gives lean protein, iron and zinc; the cream and cognac sauce makes this a rich plate for a special meal.

ingredients.prepNote: fillet; rump steak is the everyday choice

instructions: Rub the steaks with a little oil and salt, then press the crushed pepper firmly onto both sides. Leave at room temperature for 20 to 30 minutes.
Heat half the butter and the oil in a heavy pan over high heat and sear the steaks 2 to 4 minutes a side, to taste. Rest them under foil for 10 minutes.
Pour off the fat, add the cognac and flame it carefully, scraping up the browned bits. Add the white wine and reduce by half.
Add the cream and reduce by half, 2 to 3 minutes, then the brown stock, and simmer until it coats a spoon.
Off the heat, whisk in the mustard and the rest of the butter, add the steak resting juices and pour over the steaks. Serve with frites or sautéed potatoes.

recipes.name: Carbonnade Flamande
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, malty and gently sour, with beef slow-cooked in dark beer and onions, thickened by gingerbread spread with mustard.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef chuck gives protein, iron and zinc, and the long-cooked onions add a little fibre to a rich, beer-braised dish.

ingredients.prepNote: an amber or brown Flemish beer
vergeoise brune is the local sugar

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Brown the beef in the butter and oil in a heavy casserole, in batches, 4 to 6 minutes a batch, and set aside.
Soften the onions in the same pan until golden, 10 to 15 minutes, then stir in the sugar and let it melt.
Pour in the beer and scrape up the browned bits, then add the stock, thyme, bay and the beef. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour.
Spread the gingerbread slices with mustard and lay them on top, mustard side down. Cover and cook 2 to 2 1/2 hours more, until the gingerbread has melted into the sauce.
Stir in the cider vinegar, season with the salt and pepper and serve with frites.

nutritionHighlights.note: The beef carries most of it.

recipes.name: Hachis Parmentier
recipes.flavorProfile: Homely and soothing, with savoury minced beef and onions under buttery mashed potato baked to a golden, cheesy top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef gives protein, iron and zinc and the potatoes potassium; with butter and cheese it is a filling family dish rather than a light one.

ingredients.prepNote: or the leftover meat of a pot-au-feu, chopped

ingredients.cutPrep: 50 g for the onions, 50 g in thin slices on top

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Brown the finely chopped onions in 50 g of the butter.
Add the beef, the parsley, the pepper and the wine, and cook, breaking up the meat, until it is cooked through and the wine has mostly cooked away.
Spread a little of the purée in a baking dish, add the meat, then cover with the rest of the purée.
Lay the remaining butter on top in thin slices, scatter with the Gruyère and bake for about 15 minutes, until the cheese is golden.

nutritionHighlights.note: The potatoes carry most of it.
From the Gruyère and the milk in the purée.

recipes.name: Gigot d'Agneau
recipes.flavorProfile: Pink and juicy, with a browned, herb-scented crust, soft sweet garlic cloves to crush into the meat and a short pan jus.
recipes.healthBenefit: Leg of lamb gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and garlic and herbs bring flavour without much added fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 whole head, cloves separated and left unpeeled

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Season the lamb all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a roasting dish or cast-iron pot and brown the lamb on every side, 8 to 10 minutes.
Scatter the unpeeled garlic, thyme and rosemary around it and roast, basting often: 12 minutes per 500 g (about 50 minutes) for pink, 15 minutes per 500 g (about 60 minutes) for medium.
Lift out the lamb, cover with foil and rest for 20 to 30 minutes. Set the garlic aside.
Put the dish over high heat, pour in the water and scrape up the browned bits, skim off the fat and reduce by half, 3 to 5 minutes.
Carve the lamb and serve with the jus, the garlic cloves to squeeze out, and flageolets.

citations.source: 750g, Gigot d'agneau à l'ail au four

recipes.curationNote: 750g, Gigot d'agneau rôti et son jus for every amount and step; for 6 like ours: 2 kg leg, 1 head of garlic, 5 cl olive oil, 1 sprig each of thyme and rosemary, 10 cl water for the juices, salt and pepper to taste, 190°C at 12 to 15 minutes per 500 g; matches, with the usual salt and pepper amounts.

recipes.name: Choucroute Garnie
recipes.flavorProfile: Tangy, smoky and generous, with sauerkraut braised soft in Alsace wine and juniper under a pile of smoked pork, sausages and potatoes.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sauerkraut brings vitamin C and fibre (its live cultures do not survive the long braise), and the pork gives plenty of protein in a dish that is rich and salty, so it suits a shared feast.

ingredients.prepNote: a dry Alsace white (Riesling or Sylvaner)

instructions: Put the smoked belly, shoulder, salt belly and smoked sausages in cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes. Rinse and drain.
Rinse the sauerkraut in several changes of cold water and drain without squeezing. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large casserole, soften the onion in the lard for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, bay, clove, juniper, peppercorns and seeds.
Spread half the sauerkraut in the pot, lay the blanched meats on it and cover with the rest. Pour in the wine and enough water to reach the top of the sauerkraut.
Bring to a simmer, cover and bake for 2 hours, adding water if it starts to dry.
Boil the potatoes in salted water, 20 to 25 minutes. Prick the Strasbourg sausages and heat them in hot, not boiling, water for 8 to 10 minutes.
Slice the meats, pile the sauerkraut on a warm platter and arrange the meats, sausages and potatoes on top. Serve with mustard.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the smoked pork and sausages.

citations.source: 750g, La meilleure façon de faire une choucroute garnie

recipes.curationNote: 750g gives quantities, the blanching and the 2 hour oven braise; Wikipédia confirms lard or goose fat, Alsace wine and the three sausages. Shoulder, salt belly and the sausages are not in the database.

recipes.name: Tartiflette
recipes.flavorProfile: Molten and mountain-hearty, with golden potatoes, onions and smoky lardons under a whole Reblochon melted to a bubbling, nutty crust.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes give potassium and Reblochon calcium and protein, but with a whole cheese and lardons this is a rich dish for a cold day, best with a green salad.

ingredients.cutPrep: firm, peeled and cut in chunks

ingredients.prepNote: a Savoie white such as Apremont

instructions: Cook the lardons and onions in a large pan for 3 to 5 minutes, until they start to brown.
Add the potatoes and cook over medium heat, turning often, for 20 minutes, until tender.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pour in the wine and cook 5 minutes more. Season with pepper and nutmeg; no salt is needed.
Halve the Reblochon horizontally and cut one half into small pieces.
Mix the potato mixture with the small pieces in the dish and lay the other half on top, rind up.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden. Serve hot with a green salad.
recipes.curationNote: Reblochon de Savoie, Tartiflette for every amount and step; serves 4: 1 Reblochon, 1 kg firm potatoes, 200 g smoked lardons, 2 large onions, 10 cl white wine, pepper, optional nutmeg, no salt, 200°C for 15 to 20 minutes. Followed alone in place of the blend with 750g.

recipes.name: Petit Salé aux Lentilles
recipes.flavorProfile: Earthy and smoky, with peppery green lentils soaking up the juices of salt pork and sausage.
recipes.healthBenefit: Green lentils bring fibre, plant protein, folate and iron beside the pork; the salted meat makes it salty, so no salt goes in until the end.

ingredients.prepNote: one ladle of the pork cooking broth; the lentil water is drained away

instructions: Soak the salt pork in cold water for 2 hours, changing the water a few times.
Put the pork in a pot of fresh cold water with the clove-studded onion, thyme, bay and peppercorns. Bring to a boil, skim and simmer gently for 1 3/4 hours.
Meanwhile soften the other onion, the garlic, carrot and celery in the lard for 5 minutes. Add the lentils and three times their volume of cold water and simmer 20 to 30 minutes, until just tender.
Prick the sausages and add them to the pork for the last 30 minutes.
Drain the lentils, add the meats and a ladle of the pork broth and simmer together for 10 minutes. Taste first: the salted cuts usually season it enough. Serve with mustard.

recipes.name: Lapin à la Moutarde
recipes.flavorProfile: Tangy and creamy, with tender rabbit and mushrooms in a mustard and crème fraîche sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rabbit is a lean meat rich in protein and vitamin B12, and the mushrooms add selenium; the cream keeps the sauce rich but the portion modest.

ingredients.prepNote: a farmed rabbit is the usual choice

instructions: Melt the butter in a casserole and brown the rabbit pieces on every side, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the sliced onions and mushrooms and let them soften for 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock, stir in the mustard and add the thyme. Cover and simmer gently for about 40 minutes, until the rabbit is tender.
Stir in the crème fraîche, season with the salt and pepper, take out the thyme and serve.

citations.source: 750g, Lapin à la moutarde de grand-mère

recipes.curationNote: 750g, Lapin à la moutarde de grand-mère for every amount and step; 1 rabbit, 200 g mushrooms, 3 tbsp strong mustard, 20 g butter, half a stock cube in 20 cl water, 1 tbsp thick crème fraîche, 2 onions, 1 thyme sprig, salt and pepper to taste; the page says 6 people for the one rabbit, ours keeps the one rabbit for 4. The stock stays the fond blanc.

recipes.name: Filet Mignon de Porc à la Normande
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender and mellow, with pork fillet in a creamy cider sauce lifted by calvados, mushrooms and a little smoky bacon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork tenderloin is lean and rich in protein, thiamine and selenium, and the cream sauce makes it a rich, comforting plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: in 2 cm (3/4 in) medallions or whole

instructions: Fry the lardons in a heavy pan over medium heat until they give up their fat, then brown the pork in that fat over medium-high heat, 5 to 8 minutes, and lift it out.
Add the onion and mushrooms to the pan and cook until golden, 6 to 8 minutes.
Return the pork, pour in the calvados and flame it carefully.
Add the cider, cover and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning the pork once, until just cooked through (145°F, 63°C in the centre).
Lift out the pork, stir the crème fraîche into the pan and boil 2 to 3 minutes to thicken. Season with the salt and pepper, slice the pork and serve under the sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pork is one of the richest sources.

citations.source: 750g, Filet mignon de porc à la normande

recipes.curationNote: 750g, Filet mignon de porc à la normande for every amount and step; for 4 like ours: 700 g pork fillet, 15 cl cider, 5 cl calvados, 10 cl crème fraîche, 50 g smoked lardons, 100 g button mushrooms, 1 onion, salt and pepper to taste; no butter and no apples.

recipes.name: Ratatouille
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet summer vegetables, each still tasting of itself, held together by garlicky tomato and a breath of Provençal herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: A dish made almost entirely of vegetables and olive oil, so it brings fibre, potassium, vitamin C and the carotenoids of ripe tomatoes and peppers.
instructions: Cook each vegetable separately in a little of the olive oil over medium-high heat: the eggplant 6 to 8 minutes, the zucchini 4 to 5 minutes, the peppers 5 to 6 minutes, until lightly coloured. Set each aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion and garlic in a little more oil for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 5 to 10 minutes until saucy.
Return all the vegetables, add the herbes de Provence, salt and pepper and stir gently.
Cover and cook over very low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, or bake at 325°F (160°C) for 25 to 30 minutes, until everything is tender but still holds its shape.
Serve warm, at room temperature or cold the next day, when it tastes even better.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggplant, zucchini and peppers.
Mostly from the peppers and tomatoes.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Ratatouille traditional recipe

recipes.curationNote: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Ratatouille traditional recipe for every amount and step; serves 6: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 eggplant, 2 zucchini, 1 red and 1 green pepper, 6 tomatoes, 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp herbes de Provence, salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Gratin Dauphinois
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender layers of potato baked slowly in garlicky, nutmeg-scented milk and cream until the top turns golden and the inside is meltingly soft.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes bring potassium and vitamin C and the milk adds calcium; the cream makes it rich, so it suits a modest portion beside roast meat and a green vegetable.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled, sliced 3 mm (1/8 in), not rinsed

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 cloves, 1 halved for rubbing the dish, 2 crushed

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Rub a shallow baking dish with the cut garlic, then butter it.
Bring the milk and cream to a simmer with the crushed garlic, thyme, rosemary, bay, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Take off the heat and leave to infuse for 5 minutes, then lift out the herbs.
Lay the potato slices in the dish in overlapping layers and pour the hot milk over them so it just reaches the top layer.
Cover with foil and bake for 50 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until the top is golden and a knife slides through easily.
Rest 10 minutes before serving. There is no cheese and no egg in a gratin dauphinois.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Potatoes dauphinoise

recipes.name: Purée de Pommes de Terre
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, light and buttery mashed potato, loosened with warm milk and lifted with a grating of nutmeg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes give potassium, vitamin C and filling starch, and milk adds calcium; the butter makes it rich, so a little goes a long way.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold salted water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 20 to 25 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Drain well and pass the potatoes, still hot, through a ricer or food mill back into the pot. Never use a blender, which turns them gluey.
Over low heat, beat in the cold butter a few cubes at a time with a wooden spoon or whisk.
Add the warm milk little by little until the purée is smooth and soft. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg and serve at once.

citations.source: 750g, La meilleure recette de purée maison
750g, Purée de pommes de terre à l'ancienne

recipes.curationNote: 750g, La meilleure recette de purée maison for every amount and step; serves 4: 1 kg floury potatoes, 150 g butter, 200 g whole milk, coarse salt, salt, white pepper and nutmeg to taste; our 1.2 kg is within range.

recipes.name: Pommes Anna
recipes.flavorProfile: A golden, crisp-edged potato cake of thin buttery layers, soft and tender in the middle when cut into wedges.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes bring potassium and vitamin C; this is a buttery dish, so it is best as an occasional side to grilled meat with vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled, sliced 2 mm (1/16 in), not rinsed after slicing

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Brush an ovenproof cast-iron pan or a charlotte mould generously with clarified butter.
Arrange the slices in overlapping circles over the base and up the sides, then build five or six layers, brushing each with clarified butter and seasoning with salt and pepper.
Press down firmly, cover with foil or parchment and bake 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until the edges are deep golden and a knife slides through.
Rest 10 minutes, then turn out onto a plate and cut into wedges. Serve with grilled meat.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little from the clarified butter.

recipes.curationNote: Wikipédia: firm potatoes and plenty of butter only, layered five or six deep in a charlotte mould, covered in a hot oven for 25 minutes, attributed to Dugléré at the Café Anglais around 1870. English Wikipedia names clarified butter. Olive Magazine gives slice thickness and the 190 to 220°C range; its garlic and pink peppercorns were left out.

components.note: 3 tbsp of garlic and parsley, chopped together

recipes.name: Pommes Sarladaises
recipes.flavorProfile: Potato slices fried slowly in duck fat until crisp at the edges and soft inside, tossed at the end with garlic and parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes bring potassium and vitamin C; frying in duck fat makes this a rich treat best kept for a special meal.

ingredients.cutPrep: 5 firm potatoes, peeled, sliced 3 mm (1/8 in)

instructions: Rinse the potato slices, then dry them well in a cloth.
Melt the duck fat in a large heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and fry 15 to 20 minutes, turning often, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Scatter over the persillade, season with salt and pepper, cover and cook 5 minutes over low heat so the garlic perfumes the potatoes.
Serve hot with confit de canard or a magret.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potatoes and the fresh parsley.

recipes.curationNote: 750g, Pommes de terre sarladaises for every amount and step; 5 firm potatoes, 1 tbsp duck fat, 3 garlic cloves, parsley, salt and pepper to taste; fried 15 to 20 minutes then 5 minutes covered.

recipes.name: Pommes Frites
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick-cut fries, fluffy inside with a crackling golden shell, salted the moment they leave the fat.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes give potassium and vitamin C, but deep frying makes this a treat; beef tallow is the traditional fat in the north and in Belgium.

ingredients.cutPrep: floury potatoes such as Bintje, cut in 1 cm (1/2 in) sticks

ingredients.prepNote: heat about 2 litres for the frying bath; roughly this much stays in the fries

instructions: Rinse the cut potatoes in cold water, then dry them thoroughly in a cloth.
Heat the tallow to 300°F (150°C). Fry the potatoes in two batches for 6 to 10 minutes, until soft but still pale. Drain and leave to cool 10 to 20 minutes.
Just before serving, heat the fat to 355 to 375°F (180 to 190°C) and fry again in batches for 2 to 5 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Drain, salt straight away while they are still steaming, and serve.

citations.source: Le Routard, Recette des véritables frites ch'tis

recipes.curationNote: Le Routard: 1 kg floury potatoes, 1 cm sticks, 150°C for 10 minutes then 180°C for 5. Wikipédia: beef tallow as the traditional fat, a first bath of 127 to 140°C, a rest, then 175 to 190°C. The ranges cover both. Only the fat absorbed is counted, not the whole bath.

recipes.name: Petits Pois à la Française
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet young peas melted with soft lettuce, spring onion and a little smoky bacon in a buttery, barely-there sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Peas bring plant protein, fibre, folate and vitamin K, and the lettuce adds more greens to a light side dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: shelled from about 1 kg (2 lb) in the pod
or a sprig of fresh savory

instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy casserole over low heat and soften the spring onions for 5 minutes.
Add the lardons and cook 5 minutes more, without browning hard.
Add the peas, lettuce, savory, pepper and the water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently 10 to 15 minutes, until the peas are tender and only a little liquid remains. Taste for salt, since the bacon is salty, and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: Peas and lettuce both carry it.

citations.source: 750g, Le secret du chef Éric Fréchon pour les petits pois à la française

recipes.curationNote: Fréchon: 1 kg peas in the pod, 30 g butter, 2 spring onions, smoked bacon, a lettuce heart and savory. The 750g home recipe gives the order (onion, then lardons, then lettuce and peas with water, covered). Its stock cube was left out; water and the bacon season it.

recipes.name: Carottes Vichy
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin carrot rounds cooked slowly until tender and lightly glazed with butter and a little sugar, finished with fresh parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Carrots are one of the richest sources of beta-carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A, and the butter in the glaze helps it be absorbed.

ingredients.prepNote: plain water with a tiny pinch of baking soda is the usual stand-in

instructions: Put the carrots in a wide pan with the butter and sugar and pour in enough Vichy water to just cover them.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 30 to 40 minutes, until the carrots are tender.
Uncover for the last 5 to 10 minutes and let the liquid reduce until it coats the carrots in a light, shiny glaze.
Taste before adding any salt, since the mineral water seasons them, then scatter with parsley and serve.
recipes.curationNote: 750g gives 1 kg carrots in 3 mm rounds, about 1 litre of Vichy water, 75 g butter, a teaspoon of sugar and 40 to 45 minutes covered. CooksInfo confirms butter, sugar, parsley, no added salt, and plain water with a pinch of baking soda as the stand-in.

recipes.name: Endives Braisées
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole endives browned in butter until caramelised, then braised soft, so their bitterness turns mellow and sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: Endive is low in calories and brings folate, vitamin K and a little fibre; the butter and sugar glaze is small per serving.

ingredients.cutPrep: 8 heads, a thin slice cut off the base

instructions: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and lay the endives side by side. Brown them 2 to 3 minutes a side.
Sprinkle over the brown sugar and let it caramelise for 2 minutes, turning the endives to coat them.
Add the lemon juice and the veal jus, season, cover and braise over low heat 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Uncover and let any liquid reduce to a glaze for 2 to 3 minutes. Serve with roast meat or fish.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Baked endives with ham

recipes.curationNote: 750g gives brown sugar, lemon juice and a little veal jus with butter. Géraldine confirms the browning in butter then 15 to 20 minutes braising with a little liquid (she uses honey and water). The jus points at the fond brun.

recipes.name: Lentilles du Puy
recipes.flavorProfile: Small green lentils that hold their shape, earthy and peppery, cooked with lardons, carrot, onion and herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lentils bring plant protein, fibre, iron and folate, and the Puy lentil is known for cooking quickly and staying firm.
instructions: In a heavy pot, cook the lardons over medium heat until lightly golden, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the carrot and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the lentils, the clove-studded onion and the thyme and bay. Pour in the cold water and bring slowly to a simmer.
Simmer gently, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still whole. Salt only in the last 5 minutes.
Drain off any extra liquid, lift out the onion and herbs, season with the pepper and serve with sausages, salt pork or fish.

nutritionHighlights.note: Lentils are one of the best plant sources.

citations.source: 750g, Lentilles vertes du Puy à la saucisse de Morteau
750g, Ragoût de lentilles vertes du Puy

recipes.name: Flageolets
recipes.flavorProfile: Pale green beans cooked until creamy inside, scented with thyme, bay and garlic and glossed with a little salted butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: Flageolets bring plant protein, a large amount of fibre, folate and iron, and soaking them overnight makes them easier to digest.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in cold water at least 12 hours, drained

instructions: Put the soaked beans in a large pot with the carrot, clove-studded onion, garlic, thyme and bay. Cover generously with cold water.
Bring slowly to a simmer and cook gently, partly covered, 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until tender.
Add the salt only three quarters of the way through, so the skins soften fully.
Drain, lift out the aromatics, and toss the beans in a sauté pan with the salted butter, or with 2 tablespoons of the roasting juices from a gigot. Serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: Flageolets are a good plant source.

citations.source: 750g, Pourquoi accompagne-t-on l'agneau de flageolets à Pâques

recipes.name: Tian Provençal
recipes.flavorProfile: Rings of zucchini, eggplant and tomato baked slowly in olive oil and herbs until soft, sweet and lightly charred at the edges.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all vegetables and olive oil, so it brings fibre, potassium, vitamin C and the carotenoids of baked tomato.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Oil a shallow earthenware or ceramic dish and scatter the garlic over the base.
Stand the vegetable rounds upright in the dish, alternating zucchini, eggplant and tomato, packed tightly in rows or a spiral.
Drizzle with the rest of the olive oil and sprinkle with herbes de Provence, salt and pepper.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes, then uncover and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and browned at the edges.

citations.source: La Cuisine de Géraldine, Vegetable tian à la provençale

recipes.curationNote: Géraldine gives quantities, 200°C and 20 minutes covered then 20 to 25 uncovered. Wikipédia confirms the layered vegetables in a glazed earthenware dish and slow baking; the goat cheese it mentions is optional and left out to match Géraldine.

components.note: 4 tbsp of garlic and parsley, chopped together

recipes.name: Champignons à la Provençale
recipes.flavorProfile: Mushrooms seared hard in olive oil until browned and meaty, then tossed with garlic and parsley so they smell of the south.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mushrooms are low in calories and bring B vitamins, potassium and selenium; olive oil carries the garlic and parsley.

ingredients.cutPrep: wiped clean, quartered or thickly sliced

instructions: Heat a large frying pan very hot and add the mushrooms in a single layer, in two batches if needed. Cook dry for 4 to 6 minutes, until their water has gone.
Add the olive oil and keep cooking over high heat 5 to 7 minutes, until the mushrooms are well browned.
Scatter over the persillade, season with the salt and pepper and toss for 1 minute, just until the garlic smells sweet. Serve hot.

citations.source: Île aux épices, Champignons à la persillade

recipes.curationNote: Île aux épices, Champignons à la persillade for every amount and step; for 6 like ours: 1 kg mushrooms, 2 tbsp olive oil, persillade (fresh: garlic and parsley), salt added late and pepper, no amounts for salt or pepper.

recipes.name: Aligot
recipes.flavorProfile: Velvety, garlicky mashed potato beaten with fresh tomme until it stretches in long ribbons from the spoon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes bring potassium and the tomme adds protein and calcium; with cream and cheese it is a rich mountain dish, usually served with a sausage.

ingredients.prepNote: in place of tomme fraîche de l'Aubrac (or Laguiole), which the database does not hold

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 clove, peeled, in the cooking water
coarse salt, in the cooking water

instructions: Put the potatoes in cold water with the salt, garlic, thyme and bay, bring to the boil and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender. Drain well and lift out the thyme and bay, keeping the garlic.
Mash the potatoes and garlic, still hot, in the pan over low heat with the butter.
Beat in the crème fraîche in two additions and season with nutmeg and pepper.
Add the tomme a handful at a time, beating hard with a wooden spoon in a figure-of-eight for 5 to 10 minutes, until the aligot is smooth, glossy and stretches in long ribbons.
Serve straight away, traditionally with Toulouse sausage.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomme and crème fraîche.

citations.source: 750g, La meilleure façon de faire de l'aligot

recipes.curationNote: 750g, La meilleure façon de faire de l'aligot for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours; butter kept from Wikipédia's description of the dish.

recipes.name: Épinards à la Crème
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender wilted spinach, chopped and folded into butter-softened shallot and thick crème fraîche, with a grating of nutmeg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Spinach brings folate, vitamin K, vitamin A and magnesium; the cream makes it soft and rich, so it sits well beside fish or eggs.
instructions: Put the washed spinach in a large pan with only the water clinging to its leaves and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until wilted.
Drain, cool under cold running water, squeeze out the water firmly with your hands and chop roughly.
Soften the shallot in the butter over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes. Add the spinach and nutmeg and stir 2 minutes.
Stir in the crème fraîche and warm through 2 to 3 minutes until creamy. Serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: Spinach is one of the richest sources.

recipes.name: Salade Niçoise
recipes.flavorProfile: Ripe tomatoes, cucumber, young broad beans, artichoke and green pepper with anchovies, black olives, capers, egg and basil, dressed only with olive oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw vegetables bring vitamin C and fibre, the eggs and anchovies bring protein and the anchovies add omega-3 fats, all carried by olive oil.

ingredients.cutPrep: 12 small artichokes, trimmed and sliced into thin rounds
ingredients.prepNote: weight estimated, about 40 g each once trimmed

ingredients.cutPrep: 6 small white onions, in thin rings
1 clove, halved, for rubbing the bowl

ingredients.prepNote: or 300 g tuna steak, not both
to taste, part for the tomatoes

instructions: Hard-boil the eggs, cool them in cold water, peel them and cut them in quarters or slices.
Quarter the tomatoes, salt them lightly and leave them to drain.
Cut the anchovies into pieces about the size of the egg pieces. Peel and thinly slice the cucumber, cut the peppers and onions into thin rings and slice the artichokes into thin rounds.
Rub a large salad bowl with the cut garlic and put in everything except the tomatoes: cucumber, broad beans, artichokes, peppers, onions, eggs, anchovies, olives and capers.
Drain the tomatoes, salt them lightly once more and add them to the bowl.
Mix the olive oil with the basil, pepper and a little salt, pour it over the salad and chill it before serving. Nothing is cooked except the eggs, and there is no vinegar.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the raw tomatoes and peppers.

recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks, Cookbook: Niçoise Salad (CC BY-SA) for every amount and step, 6 servings: 10 tomatoes, 1 large cucumber, 200 g young broad beans or green beans, 12 small artichokes, 2 green peppers, 6 small white onions, 6 basil leaves, 1 garlic clove, 3 eggs, 12 anchovy fillets or 300 g tuna, 100 g olives, a handful of capers, 6 spoonfuls olive oil, salt and pepper.
